title: Incident play - customer recovery notes (scratch)
content:
Context / purpose:
This is my personal scratchpad for the recovery call with Acme Retail (priority P1) — goal is to capture immediate triage, clear actions with owners, and a short technical checklist we can hand off to infra. Keep compact; will convert to formal post-meeting summary after the call.

Meeting goal (30 min):
- Triage root cause hypothesis (deploy + network + model variant)
- Stabilize customer traffic to acceptable SLOs (p95 latency < 800ms)
- Agree on minimum viable rollback / mitigation and timeline
- Assign owners for 0-24h actions and 24-72h follow-ups

Quick facts I have pre-call:
- Reported at 09:10 ET: timeouts and partial responses from Redwood Hosted API (region us-east1)
- Customer using model: llama-redwood-v2-7b (quantized variant) via dedicated routing to us-east reservation pool
- Traffic spike from batch job at ~09:05, concurrency jumped from 60 -> 520
- Incidents list shows autoscale events at 09:06, several OOM signals on node gpu-*-12
- SRE page: node remediation started 09:12; some nodes restarted, backend logs show KV cache corruption warnings (rare)
- Customer impact: web checkout requests failing, revenue impact estimated high

Hypotheses (fast):
1) Autoscaler misconfigured for dedicated pool -> overloaded nodes -> OOM and degraded performance
2) Model variant/quantization edge-case triggers excessive memory use on certain sequence lengths
3) Prefix/KV cache corruption causing long tails on first-request after restart
4) Network egress congestion between us-east AZs causing retries and higher latencies

Rapid triage checklist to run during call (who / how):
- Maya: confirm customer mitigation (paused batch job? reduced concurrency?)
- Arjun (infra): check pool util, node-level OOM logs, and recent kernel upgrades (run: cloudctl pool describe --name dedicated-us-east)
- Priya (serving-runtime): examine model load traces for quantized variant and recent kernel selection logs (query: model-telemetry/llama-redwood-v2-7b)
- Ask customer to switch traffic to fallback route (if available) or reduce QPS by 70% for 15 mins

Immediate mitigations (0-2h) - propose and assign:
- Ask customer to pause scheduled batch job now (Maya -> customer contact: Sam). ETA 5-10m.
- Reduce concurrency cap on their API key to 80 for 30 minutes (Maya -> Console-> rate-limits, then tell Arjun).
- Fallback routing: shift 20% of traffic to hosted pool in us-west as warm failover (Arjun -> infra runbook, test 1 request).
- If memory OOM persists, trigger fast rollback to previous model variant (Priya -> run rollback script id: rollback/llama-v2-7b-stable).

Post-call actions (0-24h):
- Formal incident summary to customer and leadership (Maya) - include timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, ETA for full recovery. Due: within 2 hours after call.
- Deep dive ticket created: INC-4821 (Maya) -> link logs, node dumps, KV cache traces. Assign to Arjun + Priya.
- Hotfix: disable aggressive autoscaler burst policy for dedicated-us-east for next 24h (Arjun).
- Run targeted replay test with reproducer sequence lengths that triggered memory growth (Priya).
- Confirm backup KV cache and run integrity check across restarted nodes (SRE rotation).

Monitoring and success criteria (who checks):
- p95 latency < 800ms for 30m (Maya watches dashboard, SLO alerting)
- Error rate < 1% for customer keys (Arjun monitors logs, set temporary alert threshold)
- No new OOMs in node pool for 1h (Priya + infra)

If we can't stabilize within 60m -> escalate to exec-on-call and propose customer-safe rollback to previous model & pin to stable pool, plus credits conversation (Maya).

Notes to self (things to remember to document):
- Capture exact autoscaler config snapshot before change (cloudctl autoscaler get dedicated-us-east --snapshot).
- Keep copy of the customer's recent prompts / batch job manifest for replay check (ask customer for consent).
- Mention KV cache corruption warnings and whether they align with a recent binary roll (kernel / runtime bump around 02/26).

Draft language for customer update (short):
"We saw increased concurrency from a scheduled batch job which correlated with nodes experiencing OOM-like behavior in your dedicated pool. We are temporarily limiting concurrency and shifting a portion of traffic to a failover pool while we investigate. Our infra and runtime engineers are collecting logs and will follow up with a timeline for full recovery and next steps. We will share a formal incident report within 24 hours."

Follow-up meeting plan (30m, 24h):
- 1) 15m technical sync: infra + runtime share findings and confirm root cause (Arjun + Priya)
- 2) 15m customer update: present findings, proposed mitigation or rollback path (Maya)

Open questions to resolve on call: 
- Did customer change any model config or enable new quantization flags in last 48h? (ask Sam)
- Are there cross-customer autoscaler bursts at the same time? (Arjun check cluster telemetry)
- Is there any scheduled maintenance that coincided with 02/26 runtime bump? (Priya check release calendar)

Personal checklist after call (convert to formal):
- Turn this scratchpad into a tidy incident postmortem doc (confluence) with artifacts and timeline.
- Add customers affected + estimated revenue impact to the incident header.
- Schedule retrospective with infra team for autoscaler policy review.

Quick sign-off: 
Maya (owner): will draft customer email and create ticket INC-4821.
Arjun: infra lead to run pool snapshot and start failover routing.
Priya: runtime lead to validate model variant telemetry and prepare rollback.

-- end scratchpad --
